items.question: What practice must accompany worship of this circle to be effective?
items.inference: Effective worship of this circle requires sustained application of meditation.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice makes both familiar and unfamiliar languages of many forms perceptible.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard, become present.

items.question: How and where are these languages heard by the practitioner?
premises: The self is agent and recipient
items.inference: The languages are heard spontaneously by the self, for the self, and within the self.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic roles of repeated ātmanā forms are context-dependent
items.plain_english: Indeed, by oneself they are heard by oneself, for oneself, and within oneself.

rows.grounds: comparison for the practitioner; compound kāma+deva

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the described spiritual attainment?
premises: The practitioner becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair
The practitioner is likened to Kāmadeva
The likeness is as a second Kāmadeva
items.inference: The attainment yields a rejuvenated, divinely beautiful form like a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes like a second Kāmadeva.

rows.grounds: forces to be destroyed; compound vāyu+ādi
resulting state of silence; compound mūka+vat

items.question: What effect does destroying the wind and related forces have on speech?
premises: The wind and related forces should be destroyed
The subject remains like a mute
items.inference: By destroying the wind and related forces through speech, one stands silent like a mute.
uncertainties: Whether vāyvādeḥ refers to vital airs or external winds is ambiguous
items.plain_english: One should destroy the wind and such forces by speech; then he indeed stands like a mute.

rows.grounds: function of the circle; compound sainya+stambha+kara

items.question: What is the supreme power attributed to the seventh circle?
premises: It is addressed to the goddess
items.inference: The seventh circle is supreme because it has the power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme, causing the paralysis of armies.

rows.grounds: refers to the circle or context
practitioner devoted to worship and meditation; compound pūjā+dhyāna+rata

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: One devoted to worship and meditation in that circle gains the ability to see from afar.
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation in that, there is vision from afar.

items.question: What additional powers are associated with this practice for the beloved?
items.inference: The practice grants powers such as killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and related acts.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and so forth are accomplished.

items.question: What knowledge is necessary for success in this method?
premises: The eight-times-eight method must be known
items.inference: Success is possible only by knowing the eight-times-eight method.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of eight times eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the declared teaching be ascertained without doubt?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt
items.inference: The teaching should be ascertained without doubt through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, I have declared this without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The context is what emerged from Candradvīpa
items.inference: The eighth chapter concludes in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: In the work emerged from Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

rows.grounds: topic to be explained; compound yoginī+pañkti+vinyāsa

items.question: What teaching does the speaker promise to explain to the beloved?
premises: The speaker promises to tell something
The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows
items.inference: The speaker promises to explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs to the beloved.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: What collective domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
items.inference: All earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs together constitute the complete field-group.
uncertainties: Exact nuance of kṣetraka in this context is uncertain
items.plain_english: This is the complete field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are included in this comprehensive enumeration?
items.inference: The enumeration comprehensively includes innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all those born of families, and all the door-guardians are included.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among secrets been revealed?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets
Revelation is caused by that devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret among secrets has been revealed because of the recipient's devotion.
items.plain_english: Because of your devotion, the supreme secret of secrets has been revealed.

items.question: What instruction does the speaker now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The topic is worship of the siddhas
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

rows.grounds: object to be given; compound akṣara+dvaya+vinyāsa

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of two syllables be transmitted?
premises: The arrangement of two syllables is specified
items.inference: The arrangement of two syllables should be given to others.
uncertainties: The exact referent of anyanteṣu is unclear without broader context
items.plain_english: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: What claim is made about the uniqueness of this knowledge?
premises: No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain to the beautiful-eyed listener?
premises: The topic is the method of their names
items.inference: The speaker promises to explain the method of their names to the listener.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen; I shall speak the method of their names.

rows.grounds: agents who impel the family; compound kula+codaka

items.question: Who are identified as the independent impellers of the family across the four ages?
premises: They are impellers of the family
items.inference: The independent impellers of the family are identified in relation to the four ages.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of caturyuga iti is compressed and somewhat unclear
items.plain_english: O Lord, thus are the independent impellers of the family in the four ages.

origin of the teaching; compound para+udbhava

items.question: What is the extent and origin of this Kaula teaching?
premises: It has arisen from the supreme
items.inference: This Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, extends to a measure of ten crores.
uncertainties: The unit implied by daśakoṭipramāṇaṃ is not specified
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is ten crores in measure.

rows.grounds: name of the yoginī; compound icchā+ākhyā

items.question: By whose agency and will does the yoginī named Icchā operate up to Māyā?
premises: Action extends up to Māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī named Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, operates up to the limit of Māyā.
uncertainties: The precise verbal action governing māyāntaṃ is implicit
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the siddhas and by supreme will, reaches up to Māyā.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the Mothers in this context?
premises: The Mothers are the subject group
items.inference: The teaching concerning the Mothers was told again by the sky-movers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again to the Mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who conveyed the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs described as good eaters?
premises: They are described as good eaters
items.inference: The teaching was told to the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
uncertainties: The distinction between singular bhūcarī and plural bhūcarīṇāṃ is notable but contextually unclear
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told to the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
